blindSummary: This jurisdiction offers the strongest legal framework on paper in its region for trans visitors. The constitution bans discrimination based on sexual orientation; a 2015 anti-discrimination law covers gender identity; legal gender recognition is possible (medicalised); and the government attempted same-sex unions in 2024 as part of a bid to join a regional political body. Counterweights: implementation is inconsistent, political hate speech is common (a 2022 report by a local rights group found the year marked by intolerance), and the capital's Pride proceeds under protection.
blindOutOfScope: The jurisdiction's contested status is assessed separately from the neighbouring state that claims it; implementation gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): progressive protections on paper with inconsistent implementation - constitutional ban on SO discrimination; the 2015 anti-discrimination law covers gender identity; legal gender recognition possible but bureaucratically burdensome (a Constitutional Court ruling for a local trans claimant affirmed that requiring medical interventions is unconstitutional, but no self-determination-based procedure exists, forcing litigation); the constitution defines marriage neutrally but the family law restricts it to different-sex couples; the prime minister's April 2024 civil-union announcement stalled.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on this country: the prime minister said during Pride week he would do his utmost to get the civil code adopted (a 2022 parliamentary vote had gone against same-sex-couple recognition amendments); a justice-ministry working group was drafting a bill; the 2022 annual report of a local rights group found intolerance and hatred, with politicians' hate speech common during civil-code debates; an artist received death threats over a painting; Pride Week was held here under an all-acceptance slogan.

National news outlet (Jan 2019): a regional human-rights court ruling against another state in the region - holding that a surgery requirement for gender recognition violates private-life rights - is watched closely by this country's best-known trans claimant, whose own constitutional-court case challenges a refusal to change his name and gender marker; his lawyer said the neighbouring state's case could be a turning point for the trans community across the whole region.
